title: Extend persona_prompt.py to consume mood and mode
description:
Extend chatbot/soul/persona_prompt.py to consume mood state and conversation mode during prompt assembly.

Add these capabilities to the existing persona prompt builder:
- Accept an optional MoodState parameter in the prompt assembly function(s)
- Accept an optional ConversationMode parameter in the prompt assembly function(s)
- When mood is provided, inject MoodEngine.to_prompt_hints() output into the system prompt as a subtle tone directive (not a leading announcement)
- When mode is provided, inject ModeSelector.to_prompt_hints() output and adjust response parameters (length, initiative, temperature hints) accordingly
- The persona prompt must still respect the fixed personality configuration — mood and mode are modifiers, not replacements
- Backward compatible: calls without mood/mode arguments produce the same prompt as before this extension

Import MoodEngine from chatbot.soul.mood and ModeSelector from chatbot.soul.modes (do NOT import from user_state.py — user state is injected at the turn level, not the prompt level).

Before editing, inspect:
- AGENTS.md
- docs/plans_tasks.md
- This task document (task k.6)
- chatbot/soul/persona_prompt.py (the existing file)
- chatbot/soul/mood.py (produced by task k.1)
- chatbot/soul/modes.py (produced by task k.3)

Do not infer APIs, constructor signatures, function names, module locations, or service topology from the task description alone. Inspect the referenced documents and existing implementation files first, then implement against the actual repository.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in this task's allowed_write_paths. Do NOT modify any other file under any circumstance. Do NOT update documentation, READMEs, operations guides, or any code outside the listed paths. If you believe other files need updating, ignore that impulse and finish the task with only the listed files modified. Out-of-scope edits will cause the task to be rejected.
acceptance_criteria: chatbot/soul/persona_prompt.py accepts optional mood and mode parameters in its prompt assembly function(s)
Mood hints are injected subtly (not as a leading announcement) when mood is provided
Mode hints and response parameter adjustments are injected when mode is provided
Backward compatible: calls without mood/mode produce the same output as before
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: remove or rename existing prompt assembly functions
hardcode persona configuration — must be driven by existing settings
